title: Flatness of an algebra descends through a faithfully flat algebra
statement: Let $A\to B\to C$ be compatible homomorphisms of commutative rings. If $C$ is faithfully flat over $B$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $B$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 039V, special case M = C; source-library proof in WeilConjectures/Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat/Basic.lean, Module.Flat.of_flat_of_faithfullyFlat

proof.text: For an injective A-linear map u : N → P, flatness of C over A makes C ⊗[A] u injective. The flatness criterion reduces flatness of B over A to injectivity of B ⊗[A] u.
The natural tensor-cancellation equivalences C ⊗[B] (B ⊗[A] N) ≃ C ⊗[A] N and the corresponding equivalence for P intertwine C ⊗[B] (B ⊗[A] u) with C ⊗[A] u. Hence the former is injective.

Faithful flatness of C over B reflects injectivity after tensoring, so B ⊗[A] u is injective. Since u was arbitrary, B is flat over A. The existing Lean theorem proves exactly this argument without sorry.
